SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JUNE 24, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JUNE 24, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth
  Sports Scorekeepers Chase Binford and Angelyne Villacruz.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Proclamations were made as follows:

  Allstate Cerritos (Business Spotlight).

  Scott Smith (President/CEO Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  CW van der Linden expressed concern with street maintenance.

  Chris Aafedt expressed concern with traffic noise near the Sundance Homes
  development and requested potential establishment of nighttime noise and traffic
  restrictions on Bloomfield Avenue.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding lack of response to his emails directed to
  the City, the rush to adopt the City budget, and suggested cutting the City calendar
  to reduce costs.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke generally regarding the City budget.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  June 13, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of June 13, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  June 24, 2019

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated June 24, 2019
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  6/24/2019  $3,459,748.42 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period
  ending May 31, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending May 31, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of Bid No. 1365-19, a contract for traffic signal modifications at Bloomfield
  Avenue and 166th Street, Federal Project No. HSIPL-5325(017), Project No. 18401
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Reject all bids for Bid No. 1365-19, a contract for traffic signal modifications
  at Bloomfield Avenue and 166th Street, Federal Project No. HSIPL-
  5325(017), Project No. 18401, and;
  2. Direct staff to re-evaluate and modify the scope of the project, and to re-
  advertise for bids (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  June 24, 2019

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING THE SUBMISSION OF AN
  ATTESTATION OF THE VERACITY OF THE POWER SOURCE DISCLOSURE ANNUAL
  REPORT TO THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ramzi Raufdeen, Electric Utility Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Hu, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution No. 2019-13, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING THE SUBMISSION OF AN ATTESTATION
  OF THE VERACITY OF THE POWER SOURCE DISCLOSURE ANNUAL REPORT
  TO THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a request by CalMet Services for an extraordinary
  adjustment to the maximum allowable commercial solid waste management rates
  (COUNCIL).

  Bill Kalpakoff, representing CalMet Services, requested the City Council withdraw
  this item from consideration at this meeting and to table this item to a future
  agenda.

  Written correspondence in support of the request by CalMet Services for an
  extraordinary adjustment to the maximum allowable commercial solid waste
  management rates was received from the Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  June 24, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to table this item to a
  future agenda (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of a design concept by artist Ignacio Gomez and
  recommended by the Fine Arts and Historical Commission for the public art project
  that will pay tribute to the Public Safety (Sheriff and Fire) Services. The project will
  be constructed at the north entrance area of the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station generally
  located on the northwest corner of Bloomfield Avenue and 183rd Street west of
  Cerritos City Hall (APN 7025-028-905) (COUNCIL).
  (continued from the meeting of April 11, 2019)

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern with spending City funds on this matter.

  CW van der Linden expressed concern with spending City funds on this matter

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke generally regarding the proposed public safety statue.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION (DID NOT PASS): It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido,
  to approve recommendations One (1) and (2) as follows:

  1. The Fine Arts and Historical Commission recommends that the City
  Council review and approve the following:
  a. The design concept proposed by artist Ignacio Gomez as presented in
  subject report dated April 11, 2019 inclusive of the proposed public
  gathering space;
  b. Direct staff to continue to work with the artist and his design team to refine
  and modify the design concept, as needed, to ensure that the public art
  project is in conformance with the approved design concept, all applicable
  laws, building codes and design standards of the City of Cerritos;
  c. Direct staff to finalize an agreement for the construction and installation
  of the tribute to public safety public art project;
  a. Allocate the funding in the amount of $250,000 in the FY 2019/20 budget;
  d. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute the agreement for the
  tribute to public safety art project (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  June 24, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  2. Staff recommends that the City Council review and consider the following for
  approval:
  a. The revised art concept with the addition of the canine and determine if it is
  appropriate to add this element to the Tribute to Public Safety public art
  project and, if so, modify the public space in keeping with the approved
  funding;
  b. Consider the addition of the suggested modifications that will further
  enhance the public art project with the additional accent pavers and black
  granite;
  c. Authorize the City Manager to execute any necessary change orders that do
  not exceed ten percent (10%) of the total project estimate as amended
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion did not carry (1 - 4) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards
  NOES:  Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  There was no further action taken on this item.

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

10B.1. Review and consideration of support for (State Legislation) Senate Bill 5
  (Beall/McGuire/Portantino) which proposes to provide an ongoing funding
  partnership between the State of California and cities to build affordable and
  inclusive communities (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to direct staff to
  prepare a letter of support for SB 5 and send to the authors
  (Beall/McGuire/Portantino), Assembly Housing Committee, Assembly Local
  Government Committee, and copies to Senator Archuleta, Assemblymember Garcia,
  League of California Cities, Gateway Cities COG, California Contract Cities and
  Gonsalves and Son (COUNCIL):

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 24, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Pulido, Mayor Pro
  Tem Yokoyama and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed staff to provide agenda reports, commencing at
  the meeting of July 25, 2019, regarding various revenue generating options
  including a potential sales tax measure, review of all City rates, and to provide
  related information with comparable cities.

  CONSENSUS (Pulido): Directed staff to provide an agenda report regarding
  establishing an infrastructure trust fund.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session and neither Item 12A or 12B
  was discussed.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney Services

12B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Consider initiation of litigation
  Pursuant to California Government Code § 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of cases: One (1)

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned in memory of Philip H. Hickok and Margaret Mary
  “Peggy” Lee at 9:13 p.m.
